---
title: "Ship a pack in a Claude plugin"
---

A Claude plugin can carry a capt-hook pack so its hooks load in every project the
plugin is enabled for, without that project running `capt-hook init` or editing
`packs.toml`. There are two sanctioned tiers. Pick by whether the pack should
track the *repo* or track the *session*.

## Repo-scoped: `packs.toml`

This is the cc-notes model. The pack is pinned in the project's committed
`.claude/hooks/packs.toml`, so every clone hydrates the same commit and the
wiring lives in the repo. Use it when the pack encodes that repo's own
conventions.

```bash
uvx capt-hook pack add github:acme/notes@v1.2
```

`pack add` resolves the ref, caches the commit, and writes a pinned entry;
teammates run `pack update` to hydrate it. The full workflow is in
[Use packs](packs.qmd). Nothing else on this page applies to this tier — the
plugin does no per-session work.

## Session-attached: plugin `hooks.json`

This is the cc-context model. The plugin ships the pack inside itself and
registers it once per session, so it applies to whatever project the plugin is
enabled in and leaves no trace in the repo. The plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`
wires two kinds of command:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "uvx --isolated capt-hook pack attach ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks" }] }
    ],
    "PreToolUse": [
      { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "uvx --isolated capt-hook run PreToolUse" }] }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "uvx --isolated capt-hook run Stop" }] }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `SessionStart` command runs once at session start. `pack attach` reads the
SessionStart JSON from stdin, records the pack — its manifest directory and
version — under that session, and writes nothing to stdout, since SessionStart
stdout is injected into the model context. The argument is the pack root: the
directory holding `capt-hook.toml` (here a `hooks/` subtree with `hooks = "."`).
A missing or invalid manifest exits non-zero with a stderr message, so a broken
plugin fails loud at author time rather than silently loading nothing.

Every other command is the canonical `uvx --isolated capt-hook run <Event>`,
wired for each event the pack subscribes.

## Keep the run command byte-identical

Claude Code deduplicates hook commands by exact string match: two hooks that wire
the same command string for one event run that command once. A plugin that wired
`uvx capt-hook --hooks ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks run PreToolUse` produces a
different string from the captain-hook plugin's own
`uvx --isolated capt-hook run PreToolUse` — as does the pre-9.6.0 bare
`uvx capt-hook run PreToolUse` — so Claude Code runs both: two `uvx` processes
per event, and the project's `packs.toml` packs resolved and dispatched twice.

Wiring your plugin to the identical `uvx --isolated capt-hook run PreToolUse`
collapses the two plugins into one process per event. The session-attached pack
still loads inside that one process, because `pack attach` already recorded it
for the session and `run` picks it up during discovery. So keep the run command
exactly `uvx --isolated capt-hook run <Event>` (add `--async` only where
captain-hook's own `hooks.json` does), and put per-plugin configuration in the
attached pack's manifest and hooks, never in the run command's flags.

Attach records the pack once, keyed by the session id. A subagent's hook events
carry that same session id, so an attached pack loads for subagents too — the
attach at SessionStart covers the whole session, sidechains included.

## Precedence

When a pack name arrives from more than one tier, the more explicit source wins.
A `packs.toml` entry beats an attached pack of the same name: a repo that pins
`acme-notes` gets that exact commit even if an enabled plugin also attaches an
`acme-notes`, and the ambient attach is dropped. A repo that wants none of an
ambient plugin's pack declines it by name, which beats every source:

```toml
[packs.acme-notes]
disabled = true
```

The disabled entry pins nothing and resolves to nothing; it only suppresses the
pack, whether that pack would have come from a builtin, a `packs.toml` source, or
an attach. An attached pack no project pins loads normally, and its hooks follow
the same first-decision-wins dispatch as every other pack.
